title: Effect of Povidone Iodine on the Dental Implant Internal Surface Microbiome
official: Effect of Povidone Iodine on the Dental Implant Internal Surface Microbiome
summary: We hope to learn if applying antiseptic to the inside of a dental implant will decrease or alter the types of bacteria inside it which may then decrease the incidence of implant failure associated with bone loss, infection, and other complications. During your implant placement appointment, an antiseptic (povidone iodine) will be applied to the inside one of your two new dental implants, no antiseptic will be applied to your other dental implant (this is what would occur if you choose not to participate in this study), before covering both of them with a cover screw or healing abutment. You will return to the Madigan Oral \& Maxillofacial Surgery Clinic 3-6 months later when your implant hardware is removed a swab of the implants internal cavities will be collected. Your participation in this research will last up to 6 months and require one additional minute during both your implant placement and hardware removal appointments.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Active Duty Military
* 18-55 years old
* Over 6 months remaining at local duty station (Joint Base Lewis McChord)
* Will be undergoing surgery to receive at least two dental implants

Exclusion Criteria:

* Tobacco user
* Taking medications affecting soft tissue or bone healing (e.g., IV bisphosphonates)
* Metabolic disorder affecting soft tissue or bone healing (e.g., diabetes where AIC is above 7.0)
* Active periodontal disease
* Pregnant at time of enrollment (these surgeries are not typically performed on pregnant women)
* Known or suspected allergy to OR previous adverse reaction to povidone iodine
